Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female with 3-day history of dysuria, mild suprapubic cramps, malodorous urine, and one episode of visible hematuria – clinically most consistent with uncomplicated acute cystitis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging pain with urination for 3 days; mild lower-abdominal “crampy” discomfort during voiding.  
• Associated symptoms: Single episode gross hematuria today; urine “smells weird.” Denies urinary frequency/urgency, flank or back pain, fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, or bowel changes.  
• Pertinent negatives: No vaginal discharge, no recent diarrhoea.  
• Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• Allergies: Clindamycin – causes swelling (angio-edema).  
• Medications: None regular. Tried OTC bicarbonate without relief.  
• Social/Preventive: Sexually active with new boyfriend (2 mo), consistent condom use, no prior STI screen; denies smoking, drinks socially on weekends; college biology student living with friends; last menstrual period ~2–3 weeks ago, thinks pregnancy unlikely but not ruled out.

Examination:
• Tele-visit – no vitals or physical exam performed/provided.  
• No observed systemic illness.

Impression:
Most likely diagnosis: Uncomplicated acute bacterial cystitis.  
Supporting: Acute dysuria, suprapubic discomfort, malodorous urine, episode of hematuria, absence of systemic/upper-tract signs.  

Alternate considerations:  
1. Chlamydial or gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis – new sexual partner, no prior screen (medium likelihood but lack of discharge).  
2. Distal ureteric/bladder stone – hematuria/dysuria but no colicky flank pain (lower likelihood).

Plan:
• Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim 1 tablet PO BID × 3 days (per clinician).  
• Hydration advised; consider cranberry juice for symptom relief.  
• Abstain from sexual activity until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
• Safety-net: Seek care sooner if fever, flank/back pain, or feeling generally unwell (possible pyelonephritis).  
• Follow-up: Contact clinic if symptoms persist after completing 3-day course (end of week).  
• Pregnancy test recommended if any concern.  
• STI screening discussed implicitly; not arranged during call.

Quality checks
● Missing elements: No vitals, objective urinalysis, pregnancy or STI tests, detailed medication choice/dose specifics, formal follow-up date.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear history; limited by absence of physical exam and investigations; minor audio interruptions.
